featured_videos.title: Why Protein Becomes Sugar... [New 2026 Findings]
featured_videos.creator: Carnivore Squad
featured_videos.commentary: This hits on something I see people worry about constantly in our community. The gluconeogenesis myth has been floating around forever, but here's what's actually interesting: most folks are way more afraid of protein than they need to be. Your body's pretty smart about using what it needs, and the excess doesn't just magically turn into a sugar spike that tanks your progress. One commenter nailed it by pointing out that when your body does convert some protein to glucose, it's doing it on purpose because you actually need it. The real takeaway? Stop counting protein like it's the enemy and focus on what actually matters for your goals. If you want to dig deeper into the numbers, check out our guide on how much protein you actually need on carnivore.

featured_videos.title: This is my 21 Day Weigh in on Carnivore
featured_videos.creator: DJ's Food Channel
featured_videos.editorial_title: This is my 21 Day Weigh in on Carnivore
featured_videos.commentary: Three weeks in and DJ's already seeing real results, which is exactly what I tell people to expect during that initial water-loss phase. Here's the thing though: the comments are giving him the classic pushback we see everywhere, and honestly, some of it misses the point. Yes, weight loss fundamentals are calories in and out, but what carnivore does differently is make eating at a deficit *easier* because protein keeps you full longer. The "fad diet" crowd doesn't get that this isn't about restriction feeling good. it's about not feeling hungry while eating less. I'd love to see DJ's energy levels and how his hunger patterns have shifted by week 4, because that's where the real story lives. The skepticism about cholesterol is fair enough to check in on, but that's a conversation worth having with his doctor, not a reason to bail on something that's clearly working for his weight loss right now.

featured_videos.title: The #1 Meat I Rely On for Carnivore Isn’t Ribeye
featured_videos.creator: Captain Carnivore
featured_videos.editorial_title: The #1 Meat I Rely On for Carnivore Isn’t Ribeye
featured_videos.commentary: Ground beef is having a real moment in the carnivore community, and honestly, it makes total sense. The comments are full of people doing exactly what Captain Carnivore is saying, ground beef and eggs becoming the daily baseline for folks seeing actual results like psoriasis clearing up and better sleep. What's interesting is how the narrative around carnivore has gotten so fixated on premium cuts that we've overlooked the fact that ground beef contains all those nutrient-dense "scraps" most people throw away, which is basically why it works so well. If you're bouncing between different proteins trying to figure out what sticks, ground beef's versatility, cost, and real-world results might be your answer, not because it's trendy but because it actually delivers.

featured_videos.title: Parents DESTROYED for Raising "Carnivore Babies"
featured_videos.creator: Shawn Baker MD
featured_videos.commentary: The comments on this one tell the real story. Parents are reporting kids who don't get sick, who naturally regulate their own eating without the constant snacking cycle, and who have visible muscle definition at ages when most children are struggling with their weight. That's not anecdote, that's a pattern. What gets lost in the outrage is that nobody's shocked when a kid thrives on processed foods and seed oils, but mention meat and suddenly it's "dangerous." The truth is, if you want to understand what's actually happening with carnivore kids, look at the data the parents are sharing in the comments, not the fear being pushed by people who've never coached a family through this transition.

featured_videos.title: Strict Carnivore vs Relaxed Carnivore: Which One Works Better?
featured_videos.creator: Jenny Mitich
featured_videos.editorial_title: Strict Carnivore vs Relaxed Carnivore: Which One Works Better?
featured_videos.commentary: The comment section says it all: people are tired of the carnivore police. One reader nailed it. "everybody in this lifestyle needs to chill". and you see it everywhere. Strict vs. relaxed isn't about which one wins, it's about which one you'll actually stick to for the next 2 years. The real data point isn't whether dairy or potatoes derail you in theory, it's whether you quit the diet because you're miserable. That 69-year-old on OMAD and homemade electrolyte drinks found his protocol and owns it. The person who adds one yellow potato to stay on track? That's protocol too. Stop comparing and start measuring what actually works for your body. that's when the results show up.

featured_videos.title: The Carnivore Diet Doesn't Fix Everything
featured_videos.creator: Carnivore Quest
featured_videos.editorial_title: The Carnivore Diet Doesn't Fix Everything
featured_videos.commentary: This is the honest conversation we need more of. Carnivore isn't a cure-all, and the folks who get real results are usually the ones willing to say "this worked for my digestion, but I still had to address my sleep separately" or "my energy improved, but my anxiety needed different support." I've coached plenty of people who saw weight drop fast, only to hit a wall because they expected carnivore alone to fix hormonal crashes or joint pain that required other interventions. The comments here show that too. some people found relief from TMJ symptoms, others realized cutting entire food groups actually made things worse. What matters most is matching the tool to your actual problem, not expecting one approach to be the answer for everything.
